chat.author: Mike Bishop
chat.text: Technically speaking, TAPS aimed to be that abstract transport definition, didn't it?

chat.author: Andrew Newton
chat.text: Given the rise of AIs, I bet most HTTPS usage these days is not done with browsers.

chat.author: Mike Bishop
chat.text: There's a fairly consistent API interface between Qmux, QUIC, and WebTransport. It's very deliberate that you can move freely between those.

chat.author: Andrew Newton
chat.text: The IETF lost that battle. The original BCP56 said HTTP should be for browsers only.

chat.author: Kyle Rose
chat.text: This is all "worse is better". That is a defensible philosophy if you want to get things done, but you'll pay for it later.

chat.author: Kyle Rose
chat.text:
Mike Bishop said:

Technically speaking, TAPS aimed to be that abstract transport definition, didn't it?

Yes, but at L4, not L7. This is repurposing a L7 technology for something different than it was designed for.

chat.author: Kyle Rose
chat.text: FTR, I abstained. This is not my WG :-)
